"""Monthly invoices for organisations on account.

Organisations with ``pays_by_invoice = true`` (approved by Finance: schools,
the big clubs, a few charities) book without paying up front. On the 1st of
each month the worker's ``generate_invoices`` job (behind the
``org_invoicing`` flag) calls ``generate_monthly_invoices`` for the previous
calendar month, in local time:

* one invoice per organisation; one line per confirmed or no-show booking
  that *started* in the month (no-shows are charged in full),
* a "late cancellation" line for bookings cancelled inside the ADR 0012
  window -- the hirer pays price minus what a card customer would get back,
* the block-booking discount for series with 10+ sessions *in that month*,
* no VAT columns: invoice_lines.amount_pence is gross. VAT is split when the
  PDF is rendered (vat.py). See the note there.

Payment is by bank transfer, 30 days. Finance match transfers by hand in the
back office ("Mark as paid") -> ``record_bank_transfer``. No bank feed. There
was going to be one.

Invoice numbers: HP-<financial year>-NNNNNN, e.g. HP-2526-000123 for
something issued in May 2025 or February 2026 (FY 2025/26). MAX()+1 under an advisory
lock, not a sequence -- the sequence got out of step after the 2024 restore
drill and we never went back to it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta

import structlog
from psycopg import Connection
from psycopg.rows import dict_row

from hallpass.billing.concessions import BLOCK_DISCOUNT_MIN_OCCURRENCES, BLOCK_DISCOUNT_PERCENT
from hallpass.billing.errors import InvoiceStateError
from hallpass.billing.refunds import decide
from hallpass.billing.vat import split_gross, treatment_for
from hallpass.core import clock, db
from hallpass.core.audit import write_audit
from hallpass.core.money import percent_of
from hallpass.core.tz import format_local, local_day_bounds

log = structlog.get_logger(__name__)

PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS = 30
INVOICE_LOCK_KEY = 0x48500001  # "HP" + 1. Arbitrary, never change it.


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class DraftLine:
    booking_id: int | None
    description: str
    amount_pence: int


def financial_year(d: date) -> int:
    return d.year if d.month >= 4 else d.year - 1


def previous_month(today: date) -> date:
    return (today.replace(day=1) - timedelta(days=1)).replace(day=1)


def month_end(first: date) -> date:
    return (first.replace(day=28) + timedelta(days=4)).replace(day=1) - timedelta(days=1)


def _next_number(conn: Connection, issued_on: date) -> str:
    fy = financial_year(issued_on)
    prefix = f"HP-{fy % 100:02d}{(fy + 1) % 100:02d}-"
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT max(substring(number from 9)::int) FROM invoices WHERE number LIKE %s",
        (prefix + "%",),
    ).fetchone()
    n = (row[0] or 0) + 1 if row else 1
    return f"{prefix}{n:06d}"


def build_lines(bookings: list[dict]) -> list[DraftLine]:
    """Turn booking rows into invoice lines. Pure; see test_invoices_and_vat.py."""
    in_month: dict[int, int] = {}
    for b in bookings:
        if b["series_id"] is not None and b["status"] != "cancelled":
            in_month[b["series_id"]] = in_month.get(b["series_id"], 0) + 1

    lines: list[DraftLine] = []
    for b in bookings:
        when = format_local(b["starts_at"], "%a %d %b %H:%M")
        if b["status"] == "cancelled":
            decision = decide(b["price_pence"], b["starts_at"], b["cancelled_at"], closure=b["cancel_reason"] == "closure")
            charge = b["price_pence"] - decision.amount_pence
            if charge > 0:
                lines.append(DraftLine(b["id"], f"Late cancellation: {b['space_name']}, {when}", charge))
            continue

        amount = b["price_pence"]
        # Only counts this month's sessions of the series. A 12-week block that
        # straddles two months (say 6 + 6) misses the discount on both
        # invoices. HP-377, parked: "fix when someone complains". One has.
        if b["series_id"] is not None and in_month[b["series_id"]] >= BLOCK_DISCOUNT_MIN_OCCURRENCES:
            amount -= percent_of(amount, BLOCK_DISCOUNT_PERCENT)
        suffix = " (no-show)" if b["status"] == "no_show" else ""
        lines.append(DraftLine(b["id"], f"{b['space_name']}, {when}{suffix}", amount))
    return lines

    start, _ = local_day_bounds(month)
    _, end = local_day_bounds(month_end(month))
    with conn.cursor(row_factory=dict_row) as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            SELECT b.id, b.series_id, b.starts_at, b.status, b.price_pence,
                   b.cancelled_at, b.cancel_reason, s.name AS space_name, s.kind AS space_kind
              FROM bookings b JOIN spaces s ON s.id = b.space_id
             WHERE b.organisation_id = %s
               AND b.starts_at >= %s AND b.starts_at < %s
               AND b.status IN ('confirmed', 'no_show', 'cancelled')
               AND NOT EXISTS (
                     SELECT 1 FROM invoice_lines il JOIN invoices i ON i.id = il.invoice_id
                      WHERE il.booking_id = b.id AND i.status <> 'void')
             ORDER BY b.starts_at
            """,
            (organisation_id, start, end),
        )
        bookings = cur.fetchall()
    lines = build_lines(bookings)
    if not lines:
        return None

    issued_on = issued_at.date()
    number = _next_number(conn, issued_on)
    total = sum(x.amount_pence for x in lines)
    row = conn.execute(
        """
        INSERT INTO invoices (organisation_id, number, period_start, period_end,
                              total_pence, status, issued_at, due_at)
        VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, 'issued', %s, %s)
        RETURNING id
        """,
        (organisation_id, number, month, month_end(month), total, issued_at, issued_at + timedelta(days=PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS)),
    ).fetchone()
    assert row is not None
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.executemany(
            "INSERT INTO invoice_lines (invoice_id, booking_id, description, amount_pence) VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s)",
            [(row[0], x.booking_id, x.description, x.amount_pence) for x in lines],
        )
    log.info("invoice.issued", invoice_id=row[0], number=number, organisation_id=organisation_id, total_pence=total)
    return row[0]


def generate_monthly_invoices(conn: Connection, *, month: date | str | None = None, staff_id: int | None = None) -> list[int]:
    """Invoice every pays_by_invoice organisation for ``month`` (default: last month).

    Each organisation runs in its own savepoint so one bad org (usually a
    booking with no space name after a space was renamed/merged) doesn't stop
    everyone else's invoice. Re-running is safe: bookings already on a
    non-void invoice are skipped.
    """
    if month is None:
        month = previous_month(clock.today_local())
    elif isinstance(month, str):
        month = date.fromisoformat(month[:7] + "-01")
    issued_at = clock.now()
    created: list[int] = []
    with db.advisory_lock(conn, INVOICE_LOCK_KEY) as got:
        if not got:
            log.warning("invoice.run_already_in_progress")
            return []
        orgs = db.fetch_all(conn, "SELECT id FROM organisations WHERE pays_by_invoice ORDER BY id")
        for org in orgs:
            try:
                with conn.transaction():
                    invoice_id = invoice_organisation(conn, org["id"], month, issued_at)
            except Exception:
                log.exception("invoice.failed", organisation_id=org["id"])
                continue
            if invoice_id is not None:
                created.append(invoice_id)
    if staff_id is not None:
        write_audit(conn, actor_staff_id=staff_id, action="invoice.manual_run", entity="invoices", entity_id=None, detail={"month": month.isoformat(), "created": len(created)})
    return created


def record_bank_transfer(conn: Connection, invoice_id: int, *, amount_pence: int, reference: str, staff_id: int) -> dict:
    """Finance matched a bank transfer to an invoice.

    Part payments are fine (some schools pay in two halves). The invoice goes
    to 'paid' once payments cover total_pence. Overpayments are recorded as-is
    and show up in the exceptions email; there are no credit balances.
    The bank reference goes in the audit log -- payments has nowhere to keep it.
    """
    inv = db.fetch_one(conn, "SELECT id, status, total_pence FROM invoices WHERE id = %s FOR UPDATE", (invoice_id,))
    if inv is None:
        raise InvoiceStateError(f"invoice {invoice_id} not found")
    if inv["status"] in ("void", "paid", "draft"):
        raise InvoiceStateError(f"invoice {invoice_id} is {inv['status']}")
    row = conn.execute(
        "INSERT INTO payments (invoice_id, amount_pence, method, status) VALUES (%s, %s, 'bank_transfer', 'succeeded') RETURNING id",
        (invoice_id, amount_pence),
    ).fetchone()
    assert row is not None
    paid = conn.execute(
        "SELECT COALESCE(sum(amount_pence), 0) FROM payments WHERE invoice_id = %s AND status = 'succeeded'",
        (invoice_id,),
    ).fetchone()
    paid_pence = int(paid[0]) if paid else 0
    status = inv["status"]
    if paid_pence >= inv["total_pence"]:
        conn.execute("UPDATE invoices SET status = 'paid', paid_at = now() WHERE id = %s", (invoice_id,))
        status = "paid"
    write_audit(
        conn,
        actor_staff_id=staff_id,
        action="invoice.payment_recorded",
        entity="invoices",
        entity_id=invoice_id,
        detail={"amount_pence": amount_pence, "bank_reference": reference, "payment_id": row[0]},
    )
    return {"invoice_id": invoice_id, "payment_id": row[0], "paid_pence": paid_pence, "status": status}

    (the NOT EXISTS above ignores void invoices). Lines are kept for the record."""
    inv = db.fetch_one(conn, "SELECT status FROM invoices WHERE id = %s FOR UPDATE", (invoice_id,))
    if inv is None or inv["status"] != "issued":
        raise InvoiceStateError("only issued, unpaid invoices can be voided")
    conn.execute("UPDATE invoices SET status = 'void' WHERE id = %s", (invoice_id,))
    write_audit(conn, actor_staff_id=staff_id, action="invoice.void", entity="invoices", entity_id=invoice_id, detail={"reason": reason})

    """Net/VAT per line for the PDF. Computed fresh every time -- see vat.py.

    series_occurrences here is the size of the whole series, not "this
    month's share" like the block discount uses. Yes, the two disagree.

"""VAT treatment of hires.

All tariff prices are VAT-inclusive (gross). Residents only ever see one
number. Organisations get invoices, and the invoice PDF has to show net +
VAT, so we split the gross here *at render time*. invoice_lines only stores
the gross amount_pence -- we never persisted the VAT split. That matters if
the rules below change: re-rendering an old invoice gives different VAT.
(Finance keep the PDFs they sent, so in practice they'd notice.)

Rules as implemented. NOT tax advice, and Finance have not signed off the
charity bit -- read docs/billing/assumptions-vat.md before touching this:

    hirer is a registered charity         exempt   <-- ASSUMPTION, unconfirmed
    sports space, series of 10+ sessions  exempt   (the "series of lets" rule)
    everything else                       standard 20%

The series-of-lets rule is a real HMRC rule (roughly: lets of sports
facilities to the same club, 10+ sessions, at least a day apart, paid for
as a block). We apply a simplified version. The charity rule came from the
old paper booking forms ("charities: no VAT") and nobody has confirmed it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import enum
from dataclasses import dataclass

from hallpass.core.money import vat_from_gross

STANDARD_RATE_PERCENT = 20
SPORTS_KINDS = ("sports_hall", "pitch")


class VatTreatment(enum.StrEnum):
    STANDARD = "standard"
    EXEMPT = "exempt"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class VatSplit:
    gross_pence: int
    net_pence: int
    vat_pence: int
    treatment: VatTreatment


def split_gross(gross_pence: int, treatment: VatTreatment) -> VatSplit:
    """Split a VAT-inclusive amount into net and VAT, net + vat == gross.

    VAT = gross * 20/120, half-up to the penny (core.money.vat_from_gross).
    HMRC allow rounding per line or per invoice; we do it per line, so an
    invoice's VAT total can be a few pence off "total * 1/6".
    """
    if treatment is not VatTreatment.STANDARD:
        return VatSplit(gross_pence, gross_pence, 0, treatment)
    vat = vat_from_gross(gross_pence, STANDARD_RATE_PERCENT)
    return VatSplit(gross_pence, gross_pence - vat, vat, treatment)


def is_registered_charity(organisation: dict | None) -> bool:
    # kind='charity' without a number does happen (data entry). We require
    # the number; a "charity" with no number pays VAT. Arguably wrong, see
    # the assumptions doc.
    return bool(organisation and organisation.get("charity_number"))


def treatment_for(*, space_kind: str, organisation: dict | None, series_occurrences: int) -> VatTreatment:
    # ASSUMPTION (unconfirmed with Finance): registered charities don't pay VAT
    # on hires. If Finance say no, delete this branch; the query to find the
    # affected invoices is in docs/billing/assumptions-vat.md.
    if is_registered_charity(organisation):
        return VatTreatment.EXEMPT
    if space_kind in SPORTS_KINDS and series_occurrences >= 10:
        return VatTreatment.EXEMPT
    return VatTreatment.STANDARD

# VAT assumptions (not confirmed by Finance)

**Status: assumption.** Everything on this page is what the code does and
what we *believe* is right. None of it has been confirmed in writing by
Finance or the council's VAT adviser. Treat with care.

## A1. Registered charities are VAT-exempt for hires

**What the code does.** `billing/vat.py::treatment_for` returns `EXEMPT`
for any organisation with a `charity_number`. Their invoice lines show no
VAT. Card bookings aren't affected (residents pay the gross tariff price
either way; charities on card pay the same gross price — we just don't show
a VAT split to them).

**Where it came from.** The paper booking form used before Hallpass had
"Registered charities: no VAT" printed at the bottom. Tom copied the rule
across when he built invoicing in early 2024. No one checked whether the
form was right, or still right.

**Why we doubt it.** As far as any of us understand it, VAT relief for
charities is narrow and mostly about what the charity *buys* for specific
purposes; it isn't a general "charities don't pay VAT". Hiring a meeting
room is normally either exempt for *everyone* (a letting of land, if the
council hasn't opted to tax that building) or standard-rated for everyone.
Whether the hirer is a charity probably doesn't come into it. But we're
developers, not VAT advisers.

**What we've done about it.**
- Jan 2024 reporting meeting: Janet Morley (Finance) took an action to send
  us the VAT exemption rules. Chased March 2024. Chased again Oct 2024.
- Sept 2025: raised again during the finance guide review. "We'll look
  at it after year end."
- Nothing in writing yet.

**What changes if it's wrong.**
- Delete the charity branch in `treatment_for` (and its test,
  `test_charity_is_exempt`).
- Charity invoices since Feb 2024 under-show VAT. Because the VAT split is
  computed at render time (we only store gross), re-rendering will show the
  "right" VAT on the same gross total — i.e. the charity paid the right
  *amount*, we just reported the wrong *split*. Finance would need to decide
  whether that needs correcting with HMRC. Affected invoices:

  ```sql
  SELECT i.number, i.issued_at, o.name, i.total_pence
    FROM invoices i JOIN organisations o ON o.id = i.organisation_id
   WHERE o.charity_number IS NOT NULL AND i.status <> 'void'
   ORDER BY i.issued_at;
  ```

  (About 140 invoices across 9 charities as of Sept 2025.)
- If, on the other hand, the tariff for charities was *set* net of VAT on
  the assumption they'd pay none, then the gross price is wrong too. We
  don't know whether that's how the 2024 tariff was built. Ask Finance.

## A2. The "series of lets" exemption applies at 10+ sessions

We apply exemption to sports halls and pitches booked by an organisation
in a series of 10 or more. The real HMRC conditions (as we understand them)
also require the sessions to be at least a day apart, to be for the same
activity, and for the hirer to have exclusive use. We check none of those.
We also count the whole series even if sessions were later cancelled.
Probably fine for the clubs that actually do this. Not confirmed.

## A3. Meeting rooms and music rooms are standard-rated

We charge 20% on everything that isn't covered by A1 or A2. That assumes
the council has opted to tax all its community buildings. Northgate
Community Centre may be different (it was transferred from the parish
council in 2019). Unknown.

## A4. VAT on cancellation charges

Late-cancellation lines on invoices get the same VAT treatment as the
booking would have had. Some guidance treats cancellation charges as
compensation (outside the scope of VAT). We picked "same as the booking"
because it was simpler. Not confirmed.

---

If you're from Finance and reading this: a one-line email confirming or
correcting each of A1–A4 would let us take this page down.

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, timedelta

import pytest

from hallpass.billing.invoices import build_lines, financial_year
from hallpass.billing.vat import VatTreatment, split_gross, treatment_for
from tests.billing.conftest import london

SCHOOL = {"id": 7, "kind": "school", "charity_number": None}
CHARITY = {"id": 8, "kind": "charity", "charity_number": "1123456"}
UNREGISTERED = {"id": 9, "kind": "charity", "charity_number": None}


def booking(id=1, *, status="confirmed", price=4800, series_id=None, kind="sports_hall", starts=None, cancelled=None, reason=None):
    starts = starts or london(2025, 5, 6, 18)
    return {
        "id": id,
        "series_id": series_id,
        "starts_at": starts,
        "status": status,
        "price_pence": price,
        "cancelled_at": cancelled,
        "cancel_reason": reason,
        "space_name": "Northfield Sports Hall",
        "space_kind": kind,
    }


# --- VAT -------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(("gross", "vat"), [(1200, 200), (4800, 800), (1375, 229), (1, 0), (0, 0)])
def test_split_gross_standard(gross, vat):
    s = split_gross(gross, VatTreatment.STANDARD)
    assert s.vat_pence == vat
    assert s.net_pence + s.vat_pence == gross


def test_exempt_has_no_vat():
    s = split_gross(4800, VatTreatment.EXEMPT)
    assert (s.net_pence, s.vat_pence) == (4800, 0)


def test_charity_is_exempt():
    # NB this encodes an ASSUMPTION (docs/billing/assumptions-vat.md), not a
    # confirmed rule. If Finance come back and say otherwise, this test is
    # the first thing that should change.
    assert treatment_for(space_kind="meeting_room", organisation=CHARITY, series_occurrences=1) is VatTreatment.EXEMPT


def test_charity_kind_without_number_pays_vat():
    assert treatment_for(space_kind="meeting_room", organisation=UNREGISTERED, series_occurrences=1) is VatTreatment.STANDARD


def test_school_single_let_standard_rated():
    assert treatment_for(space_kind="sports_hall", organisation=SCHOOL, series_occurrences=1) is VatTreatment.STANDARD


def test_series_of_ten_sports_lets_exempt():
    assert treatment_for(space_kind="pitch", organisation=SCHOOL, series_occurrences=10) is VatTreatment.EXEMPT


def test_series_of_ten_meeting_room_still_standard():
    assert treatment_for(space_kind="meeting_room", organisation=SCHOOL, series_occurrences=12) is VatTreatment.STANDARD


# --- invoices --------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(("d", "fy"), [(date(2025, 3, 31), 2024), (date(2025, 4, 1), 2025), (date(2026, 1, 1), 2025)])
def test_financial_year(d, fy):
    assert financial_year(d) == fy


def test_confirmed_booking_one_line_with_vat():
    lines = build_lines([booking()])
    assert len(lines) == 1
    assert lines[0].amount_pence == 4800  # gross; VAT only appears on the PDF
    assert "Tue 06 May 18:00" in lines[0].description


def test_no_show_charged_in_full():
    lines = build_lines([booking(status="no_show")])
    assert lines[0].amount_pence == 4800
    assert lines[0].description.endswith("(no-show)")


def test_late_cancellation_charges_the_non_refundable_part():
    starts = london(2025, 5, 6, 18)
    b = booking(status="cancelled", starts=starts, cancelled=starts - timedelta(days=3), reason="customer")
    lines = build_lines([b])
    assert lines[0].amount_pence == 2400
    assert lines[0].description.startswith("Late cancellation:")


def test_early_cancellation_no_line():
    starts = london(2025, 5, 6, 18)
    b = booking(status="cancelled", starts=starts, cancelled=starts - timedelta(days=10), reason="customer")
    assert build_lines([b]) == []


def test_closure_cancellation_no_line_even_if_late():
    starts = london(2025, 5, 6, 18)
    b = booking(status="cancelled", starts=starts, cancelled=starts - timedelta(hours=2), reason="closure")
    assert build_lines([b]) == []


def test_block_discount_on_ten_in_month():
    rows = [booking(i, series_id=55, kind="meeting_room", starts=london(2025, 5, 1 + i, 18)) for i in range(10)]
    lines = build_lines(rows)
    assert all(x.amount_pence == 4320 for x in lines)


def test_block_straddling_months_misses_discount():
    """HP-377. Six sessions this month, six next month: no discount on either
    invoice even though the series is 12 long. Documenting, not endorsing."""
    rows = [booking(i, series_id=56, starts=london(2025, 5, 20 + i, 18)) for i in range(6)]
    lines = build_lines(rows)
    assert all(x.amount_pence == 4800 for x in lines)
